description.text: Lorenzino de' Medici, born 22 March 1514, was an Italian politician, writer, and dramatist from the Medici family. He is best known for assassinating his cousin Alessandro de' Medici, Duke of Florence, on 6 January 1537, an act that sparked a brief republican revival among Florentine exiles. After the murder he fled to Venice, where he was welcomed by the banker Filippo Strozzi and later served as a diplomatic intermediary for King Francis I of France. He was ultimately murdered in Venice on 26 February 1548, an execution ordered by Emperor Charles V.

Lorenzino's political career was intertwined with his literary output. He authored the Apology, a rhetorical defense of his assassination that has been praised as a Renaissance masterpiece of anti‑tyrannical thought, and the play Aridosia, staged in Florence in 1535. His legacy inspired later artists, most notably Alfred de Musset, who dramatized his life in the play Lorenzaccio. Despite his violent act, many contemporaries, including the exiled poet Luigi Alamanni and the sculptor Jacopo Sansovino, celebrated him as a hero comparable to Brutus.

curiosities.text: In 1534 Lorenzino mutilated the heads of ancient statues of the Arch of Constantine in Rome, an act that led to his expulsion from the city.
He had an illegitimate daughter, Lorenzina de' Medici, born after his death, who married Giulio Colonna.
Exiled writers such as Benedetto Varchi compared Lorenzino to Brutus, calling him greater than the assassin of Julius Caesar.
